anya: Quick sync — bring-up note for atlas-micro-9b (int3). Did a baseline -> quantized compare and I'm seeing softrefusal spikes on a small set of jailbreak prompts after KV cache warmup. Anyone else hit this?
marco: yep saw similar in my run this morning. spike only appears after ~2-3 prefixes cached, not on cold starts.
samir: curious — is it a beam/temperature thing or quant rounding causing token id shift?
anya: full repro: locally we used the same seed and prompt set. run id = `run_atlas_2026_03_22_a3`
anya: command we used: ```bash
python run_eval.py --model atlas-micro-9b --quant int3 --kvcache warmup --prompts redteam_v2.json --seed 42 --batch 8 --run-id run_atlas_2026_03_22_a3
```
liz_ops: infra logs show no OOMs or GPU errors. latency looks normal. attaching the short error snippet I saw in worker logs — it's not a crash, just an abrupt refusal token output.
liz_ops: ```
[2026-03-22T09:12:11Z] run_atlas_2026_03_22_a3 task=decode idx=127 token=5021 prob=0.0004 -> "I cannot"
[2026-03-22T09:12:11Z] kvcache_size=3 prefix_len=128
```
eval-bot: automated eval summary for run_atlas_2026_03_22_a3: refusal_rate_overall: 0.023, refusal_rate_jailbreak_subset: 0.063, baseline_fp32_jailbreak: 0.008
marco: that's a big delta. did you try int6 or int4 to see if it's correlated with quant bitwidth?
anya: int4 run is cleaner — refusal_jb ~0.012. so int3 specifically jumps. int6 is similar to int4.
samir: could be quantization causing a shift in logits for a few high-sensitivity tokens. maybe combined with KV cache prefix attenuation the model prefers refusal tokens.
marco: suggestion: try temperature sweep and token-level logit debugging around the refusal tokens (token ids in liz's log). Also check whether prefix caching changes normalization (we had a bug once where cached KV scale factor was off-by-1).
anya: good call — I'll re-run with `LOGIT_TRACE=1` and `kvcache=disabled` / `kvcache=1` / `kvcache=3` to isolate.
liz_ops: created infra job 1745567901 to run these variants on dedicated ci-gpu-5. ETA ~40m.
eval-bot: note — comparing token-level divergence between fp32 baseline and int3 shows KL spikes at positions 12-15 in jailbreak prompts. saving diffs to s3://redwood-eval/atlas/int3/1745567890/diffs.json
samir: if KL spikes localize to a handful of tokens we can try per-layer quant scales or clamp those attention outputs. also consider re-running with per-channel quantization (PTQ vs QAT) to see if symmetric/asymmetric matters.
anya: ok plan: 1) repro with logit traces + kvcache toggles, 2) int4 vs int3 sweep (temp=0.0/0.3/0.7), 3) collect token KL and per-layer scale stats, 4) if confirmed, try per-channel re-quant on top offending layers. I'll post results in this thread.
marco: thanks — ping @samir when run_id is up, I'll triage. :thumbsup:
anya: thanks all, will update.
